recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not reintroduce questionItemCode or item.concept for this tracker; any further naming reconsideration would require a new Patient Care decision because FHIR-10998 later superseded the naming part of this issue family.
issue_request: FHIR-10999 was a Published Patient Care issue with resolution Persuasive with Modification. It asked to rename DSTU2 Questionnaire.item.concept to questionItemCode and revise its definition; the final resolution instead required the definition "Terminology code that corresponds to this group or question (e.g. LOINC)", did not adopt questionItemCode, and noted Questionnaire.concept would be handled separately.
initial_application: SVN-imported commit 76675fcc91938801ee4e8de9ec10d2c6e1949bc8 explicitly listed #10999 and changed the then-current Questionnaire spreadsheet definition for Questionnaire.item.concept from the old confusing wording to "Terminology code that corresponds to this group or question (e.g. LOINC)". Later QA/source-refactor history preserved that meaning in the current StructureDefinition wording.
additional_context: FHIR-10998, a later Published/Persuasive same-family Questionnaire issue, renamed Questionnaire.item.concept to Questionnaire.item.code for consistency with the Coding type and other FHIR resources; commit f3f2ad2c4b57ba4d2dfbbd990363885b40b49101 applied that rename. Earlier FHIR-8986 merged Questionnaire group/question structures into recursive items, explaining the DSTU2/R3 path history. Current source/fhir.ini lists questionnaire as active, and source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml defines Questionnaire.item.code with the resolved terminology-code meaning.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because exact current-source searches found no stale Questionnaire.item.concept, questionItemCode, or old erroneous definition references in source/questionnaire, and the active StructureDefinition already conveys the approved FHIR-10999 definition on the current element.
